subject: zoology
question_text: What is a hyper-parasite? Mention the name of one hyper-parasite.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.58, VSAQ 132). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: A parasite that lives on or inside the body of
another parasite is called a hyper-parasite.
steps.why: The word 'hyper' here means one level higher, so the host of a hyper-parasite is itself a parasite — that second level is the whole idea being tested.
common_mistakes: Writing that a hyper-parasite is a very harmful parasite. 'Hyper' names the level, not the strength.
Saying it lives on a host. Its host is another PARASITE.
steps.memory_tip: Parasite on a parasite: the host of the hyper-parasite is itself living on someone else.
steps.margin_note: One line. The whole mark is in the words 'on another parasite'.

steps.label: Example
lines: It lives on Sphaerospora polymorpha, which is
itself a parasite in the urinary bladder of the
steps.why: The example only proves the point if the chain of three is written out — hyper-parasite, its parasite host, and the animal that parasite lives in.
common_mistakes: Naming only Nosema notabilis. The parasite it lives on must be named too.
Writing the two names the other way round.
steps.memory_tip: Three names in a chain: Nosema on Sphaerospora, Sphaerospora in the toad fish.
steps.margin_note: Both names, in order, and the animal at the end of the chain. Two lines.

insider_note: Only the paired names earn the second mark — an unnamed 'parasite on a parasite' example scores nothing.
